120330104.text: Hehe, guess they must be good friends, huh?

120330113.text: Hi, Ippei! Hi, Shinnojou! What are you guys doing here?

120330114.text: Oh! It's you! Thanks so much for your help last time.

120330115.text: I was just ordering some clothes when I ran into him.

120330116.text: You know these two as well?

120330117.text: Yes. They helped me and Master Kamaji out a great deal last time. I've never had the chance to say thank you properly.

120330118.text: What about you? How do you know them?

120330119.text: Also a chance encounter. Our Lady had them join us as additional guards for a goods escort in order to sneak out of Ritou undetected.

120330120.text: So we all know each other, huh! What a coincidence!

120330121.text: Ah, not exactly. We've only just met. We both came here to order some clothes and got to chatting.

120330122.text: Somehow we ended up on the topic of Master Kamaji and Lady Hiiragi's relationship... Wait... it's okay to talk about that, right?

120330123.text: It's probably fine. They've known about it for a long time already.

120330124.text: Oh yeah! Paimon remembers those two had a thing. In fact, that was why Chisato wanted us to deliver a letter!

120330125.text: That's old news though, so why's it come up now? Are they... taking the next step, or something?

120330126.text: We have reason to suspect that they'll be getting married soon.

120330127.text: Wow! That's great! They can finally make it official!

120330128.text: Of course, this is just personal speculation. They haven't announced anything, and we wouldn't dare to ask...

120330129.text: I was instructed to place an order for some formal wear for a big banquet. Turns out that Ippei received the exact same instructions as I did.

120330130.text: They're both preparing for a banquet at the same time, they're both purchasing the kind of fine wine and confectionery normally reserved for big festivals... It's hard not to put two and two together.

120330131.text: Lady Hiiragi has been in high spirits recently, and I heard she's on a diet as well... Surely it's all for the wedding.

120330132.text: This is wonderful news! But, um...

120330134.text: Oh, don't mind me. She's about to be happily married to the love of her life. I genuinely couldn't be happier for her.

120330135.text: Right? I think so, too, it's fantastic!

120330136.text: Yes, but we shouldn't let ourselves get overexcited. What if it's all a big misunderstanding? As things stand, we have no actual proof of a wedding.

120330137.text: Now, if they sent me out to deliver wedding invitations, that would be a different story...

120330138.text: Shinnojou doesn't look like he's taking this very well at all.

120330108.text: That one is Shinnojou. Back when we first arrived in Inazuma, we escorted Hiiragi Chisato out of Ritou with him. Remember? That's how we got out.

120330109.text: Next to him is Ippei, Kujou Kamaji's servant. That day when we hung out with Ei, he came and told us that Kujou Kamaji had gone missing. He was really worried.

120330111.text: Hehe, all part of Paimon's job as your guide.

subQuests.subQuestName: Meet Ayaka at the Kamisato Estate

120330201.text: This place impresses me every time I come here. It's so magnificent but still so elegant.

120330202.text: We'll just wait here. We don't want to cause any extra trouble for you.

120330204.text: Honestly, even if we did come with you, we wouldn't know what to say or do once we were inside... Hehe, so we'll just leave you to it.

120330205.text: Alright then. We won't be long.

120330401.text: Greetings, both. I have long been indebted to you on my sister's behalf. Finally, I have the chance to express my profoundest gratitude to you in person.

120330402.text: Ayaka is out today. If you are here regarding anything related to the Kamisato Clan, you are quite welcome to discuss it with me instead.

120330403.text: Oh, uh... hi... Your flattering words... flatter us. Um, please excuse the sudden... -ness of our visit, for it is most improper etiquette...

120330404.text: Hahaha, why on earth are you talking like that?

120330405.text: Well, he seems like a pretty powerful person... He's already working his way up Paimon's list of people to never mess with...

120330406.text: Look! As soon as he stands up, the whole atmosphere in the room changes and it feels like you've gotta be super polite!

120330407.text: Haha, you shower me with praise undeserved, my little guest.

120330408.text: There is no need to be quite so formal. This is a private residence, so please relax.

120330409.text: Oh, good! 'Cause that whole spiel was really tiring just now! Alright, now that that's over, Paimon's just gonna ask the question.

120330412.text: We heard a rumor that Kujou Kamaji and Hiiragi Chisato are gonna get married soon. Do you know anything about that?

120330413.text: Oh? I wouldn't have thought you'd heard about that yet.

120330414.text: As it happens, we've crossed paths with them before.

120330415.text: I see... Well, it's true. It wasn't long ago that I received the news myself.

120330416.text: The head clans of two Commissions are to become joined through marriage. This is big news, for the whole of Inazuma.

120330417.text: Since the Yashiro Commission presides over cultural and ceremonial affairs, it closely involves us, too.

120330418.text: Yes. And since the commissions are kind of the face of the Almighty Shogun to the masses, this wedding is one that we have to treat as a serious affair.

120330420.text: Ah, two true lovers becoming husband and wife. What a happy occasion!

120330421.text: It is. High-profile matrimonial links between two commissions are extremely rare, but these two truly love each other. Tradition should give way to freedom in this case.

120330422.text: Alright then. I'll be sure to pay them a visit to send the best wishes of the Kamisato Clan.

120330424.text: No need. I'll visit them personally this time.

120330425.text: Huh? But you have other things to be doing...

120330426.text: This is a marriage between the Kujou Clan and the Hiiragi Clan. The Kamisato Clan must demonstrate an appropriate level of respect.

120330427.text: The work of the Yashiro Commission is indeed multifarious. Normally, weddings and other ceremonies would come under the supervision of my sister.

120330428.text: But she is presently occupied with other matters, and I happen to have a little time to spare. This will be a good chance for me to pay a visit to the bride and groom.

120330429.text: Oh — and would you two care to join me?

120330431.text: I presume you two have a special connection with the individuals in question, or you would not be quite so interested in this matter.

120330432.text: This being the case, why not come and offer your best wishes too? Or... is my presumption incorrect?

120330433.text: Oh, it's not as interesting as you make it sound... No special connections here. Super-ordinary ones, actually.

120330434.text: We just agreed to help deliver a letter this one time, that's all... Although, wait... does that mean we helped make this wedding happen!?

subQuests.subQuestName: Talk to Thoma and Kamisato Ayato
Report back to Ippei and Shinnojou

120330604.text: They're friends of ours. Paimon will do the introductions!

120330605.text: You introduce your companions to Ayato and update Ippei and Shinnojou on the situation.

120330607.text: Well, there we have it... That's it, then. So be it.

120330608.text: Great! So our hunch was spot on!

120330609.text: It is a little inappropriate for me to have shared news of this magnitude with you. So I would be much obliged if you could keep it in strict confidence until an official public announcement is made.

120330610.text: Don't worry, Sir. We... we give you our word, we won't tell anyone about it!

120330611.text: That puts my mind at ease. Now, on the topic, we'd like to pay a visit to the Kujou Clan. Would you mind leading the way for us?

120330612.text: Of course not. I'd be honored!

120330613.text: I guess this is where I... Goodbye, then...

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the Kujou Estate and talk to Kujou Kamaji

120330701.text: Alright then. Please excuse me, I'll leave you to it from here.

120330703.text: I apologize that your impromptu visit comes at a busy time for us, Commissioner. Otherwise, you can be sure that we would've prepared a more extravagant reception.

120330704.text: I don't mean to impose, Sir Kujou. In fact, I'm not here on official business at all.

120330705.text: I heard the good news about yourself and Lady Hiiragi. What a glorious marital alliance this shall be. Given the close ties between our clans, it seemed only right that I should come and offer the Kamisato Clan's congratulations in person.

120330706.text: I'm truly honored. I hope the news didn't come as too much of a surprise...

120330707.text: Hey there! We came to congratulate you as well!

120330709.text: Since the incident with the Takatsukasa Clan, things in the Tenryou Commission have slowly started to stabilize.

120330710.text: I'm still acclimating to the position of acting head of the Clan. I just hope I'm up to the task, so I can live up to everyone's expectations.

120330711.text: You're far too modest. The public thinks very highly of you. They say you're hard-working, upright, and responsible.

120330712.text: I'm flattered, but I wouldn't have achieved anything without the support of my people. Thanks to them, everything is gradually stabilizing, and I've finally had the chance to focus a little on my personal life.

120330713.text: Hehe, well you're certainly making big progress in that department!

120330716.text: Hehe, come on now. You're embarrassing me...

120330718.text: It's perfectly alright. Please, continue. I'm quite content to listen.

120330719.text: It's a joyous occasion. Light-hearted is exactly how things should be. Really, who stays stony-faced when talking about a wedding?

120330721.text: But I am curious to know — what's your honest opinion on the whole thing? Do you think it's... too sudden?

120330722.text: Haha, of course not. Where there is true love, nothing should be allowed to stand in its way.

120330723.text: No doubt people will offer you a colorful variety of opinions. But of course, you will have factored this into your decision, and I'm sure you are prepared for whatever challenges may lie ahead.

120330725.text: So, please be confident. When your mind is made up, you ought not be worried about things for which you are already well-prepared.

120330726.text: Nevertheless, there is just one small aspect of this that puzzles me a little...

120330728.text: You've been working hard to bring the Tenryou Commission in line. This is positive, and no doubt the beginning of an important change. But on the other side of this equation, Lady Hiiragi's father, Hiiragi Shinsuke, is still in prison.

120330729.text: If you choose now, of all moments, to announce a marriage between the Hiiragi and Kujou Clans, the kinds of rumors that may begin to spread, both among the general public and in the Kanjou Commission, are not likely to be in either of your best interests.

120330731.text: Couldn't have put it better myself, Sir Kamisato. This has been my biggest concern for quite a while now.

120330732.text: Hiiragi Shinsuke is firmly against me having any contact at all with Chisato. In the past, we've always had to communicate in secret, by sending letters.

120330733.text: So although now may not look like the best timing for this marriage, it may well be the only opportunity we have.

120330734.text: ...Oh! That guy! Yeah, he acts like this sweet old man, but he was determined to make as much trouble for us as possible! Oh, he is the worst...

120330735.text: I can see where you're coming from. But you're only postponing the problem, not solving it. You will still have to face it sooner or later.

120330736.text: *sigh* Yes, I'm well aware of that. But since Chisato had the courage to ask me to marry her in spite of everything, how can I disappoint her?

120330737.text: Oh... so she proposed to you?

120330738.text: Well, sort of... She raised the idea in a letter, and after some initial hesitation, I went to meet her and have a serious conversation about our future.

120330739.text: It's funny, actually, because when I formally proposed to her in person, she denied having ever written that letter... Ah, so coy...

120330901.text: He seems busy. That must be true for anyone about to get married, right? It's a happy kind of busy, though.

120330902.text: You're right. Kujou Kamaji is on cloud nine.

120330906.text: He chalked it up to her being coy, but... that doesn't sound like the Hiiragi Chisato I know.

120330907.text: It bothers me also. But unfortunately, attempting to seek the truth of the matter would likely be fruitless.

120330909.text: Yeah, how come? Whenever we come across stuff like this on our adventures, we always find a way to get to the bottom of it.

120330910.text: I see. So that's how adventurers think.

120330911.text: In my opinion, we face two obstacles in this case. Firstly, we have very little information to go on, and I must be cautious about taking a stance. This makes it difficult to investigate.

120330912.text: Secondly, and more importantly, the person involved doesn't seem to care.

120330913.text: If we intervene without his blessing, good intentions may lead to catastrophic results.

120330914.text: You do have a point... Kamaji doesn't seem worried at all.

120330915.text: Everything in the world is intertwined. What looks like a simple outcome is often the result of multiple conflating reasons.

120330916.text: Seeking the full truth would be a long and laborious process. It would be inefficient.

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the Hiiragi Estate in Ritou

120330801.text: I know it's not an easy path ahead, but this is my responsibility.

120330802.text: I need to give her a reason to be confident in me.

subQuests.subQuestName: Talk to members of the Kanjou Commission

120331001.text: There is still much to prepare for the wedding.

120331002.text: Should we also invite some prominent business leaders who frequently visit Ritou?

120331003.text: At the very least we should send them invitations.

120331004.text: I agree... Ah, hello there, Yashiro Commissioner.

120331005.text: To what do we owe the honor on this fine day?

120331006.text: As it happens, I'm here regarding the same wedding I believe I heard you discussing just now. I come bearing the felicitations of the Kamisato Clan.

120331007.text: Would Lady Hiiragi happen to be available at this moment?

120331008.text: Our lady is entertaining guests right now, and we're not entirely sure how long she will be.

120331009.text: But please, do come in. We will arrange some tea and snacks for you and your attendants.

120331010.text: Hey! Paimon is not an attendant!

120331011.text: You misunderstand. These two are dear friends.

120331013.text: We don't wish to impose. We'll just wander around in the general area.

120331014.text: Apologies for the interruption while you're busy with preparations. Please let us know once Lady Hiiragi is available.

120331015.text: Nonsense, Commissioner, no imposition at all. This wedding is a joyful occasion, and all the other clans who serve the Hiiragi Clan are most delighted for them indeed.

120331016.text: We're merely doing the best we can to make this wedding as grand an affair as possible.

120331017.text: When the time comes, we'll invite everyone in the clan and even the general public to attend.

120332001.text: Your review seemed pretty positive. But Paimon still thinks there are better combinations...

120332002.text: Taste is your key concern, yes?

120332003.text: Obviously! Tasty food and drinks are some of life's most important pursuits.

120332004.text: Well said. If I could say the same was true for me, I believe I'd be a very content man.

120332005.text: In other words, you have too many other things to worry about?

120332006.text: Yes. No one has unlimited energy, and I try to conserve mine for the things that really count. To create some mental breathing room, I try not to overthink the less-critical matters.

120332007.text: Having my sister attend public events in my stead and having Thoma as housekeeper has also been a great help, and allowed me to focus.

120332008.text: We're just passing the time here though, right? Is there anything else to think about than what we're doing right now?

120332010.text: Let's continue this discussion somewhere else.

120332011.text: I noticed something before we left the Hiiragi Clan's residence.

120332014.text: No, it was just a small detail. I was curious to know their thoughts on the wedding, so I asked them about it.

120332015.text: Naturally, they responded that all other clans are happy for the Hiiragi Clan...

120332018.text: Hiiragi Shinsuke is still in prison, meaning the Kanjou Commission is the least stable in the Tri-Commission.

120332019.text: Hiiragi Chisato is the sole remaining pillar of her clan, but now she plans to marry into the Kujou Clan. If I belonged to one of the assisting clans to the Hiiragis, I would not be feeling optimistic about the future.

120332020.text: But they didn't mention a word about that, they simply said they were delighted for them. These are not unintelligent people... I highly doubt it is because they simply do not realize.

120332021.text: Hmm, I guess it is a bit strange...

120332022.text: I imagine they didn't want to discuss family issues in front of outsiders. But still, the more I think back over that conversation, the more it doesn't sit right.

120332023.text: Keep a close eye on them, Hisashi.

120332025.text: Whoa! Where did you come from!?

120332026.text: This is one of my most trusted members of the Shuumatsuban. He's been quietly watching out for us this whole time.

120332028.text: Keep a close watch on the clan representatives we met today.

120332029.text: Well received. I'm on the case.

120332030.text: Oh, and I almost forgot. That milk I just had — please order one more and deliver it to Thoma.

120332201.text: Hi! Nice to see you again, Chisato!

120332202.text: I heard that Sir Kamisato had brought some guests, but I didn't know it was you two.

120332203.text: It's been a while, Lady Hiiragi. How have you been faring?

120332204.text: This is a rare privilege, Sir Kamisato. It is not often that I have the chance to meet you, let alone here in the comfort of my own home. I'm doing very well indeed, thank you.

120332205.text: You must be so busy. Thank you so much for taking the time to come and congratulate Kamaji and I, it really means a lot.

120332206.text: But of course. The Tri-Commission are the servants of the Shogun, and we should look out for one another. In fact, we visited Sir Kujou just now. It's clear that he's very much looking forward to the wedding.

120332207.text: Perhaps his joy is infectious, for I am now feeling rather elated myself. I sincerely wish you a joyful wedding and a blissful marriage.

120332208.text: Thank you for your kind words.

120332209.text: This was not an easy decision to make. We will both have to work harder from now on.

120332210.text: I'm sure the news will cause something of a stir. But come what may, we will stand as one and face whatever the future throws at us together.

120332211.text: Sounds like things are pretty tough for you, Chisato.

120332212.text: Yes... To be honest, I'm still a little nervous about it all...

120332213.text: But Kamaji has been so supportive. His promises have comforted me a lot.

120332214.text: It sounds like you have some considerable reservations, Lady Hiiragi.

120332215.text: ...Yes, well... There are so many things I need to consider.

120332216.text: In case you were wondering, I was not actually entertaining VIPs just now. I was in fact meeting with one of the Kanjou Commission's officers, Shinnojou.

120332218.text: Mm-hmm. He charged in all of a sudden and said that he had something very important to tell me.

120332219.text: He didn't mince his words. Basically... he doesn't want me to marry Kamaji.

120332221.text: He has always been a calm and contained person who never acts out of line. I was quite shocked to see him so agitated.

120332222.text: But despite all that, what he was saying made a lot of sense. He thinks that now is a bad time for this wedding to happen.

120332223.text: He pointed out that I am like the final pillar propping up my clan. If I marry into the Kujou Clan, that pillar is taken away. There will no longer be a voice of authority in the Hiiragi Clan, and it could be a disastrous move for my personal image, too...

120332224.text: It's just two families becoming one big family though, right? What's the big deal?

120332225.text: Traditionally, in Inazuma, clan affiliation influences every facet of life.

120332226.text: After the wedding, Lady Hiiragi will belong to the Kujou Clan. The Kanjou Commission's attitude toward you may undergo some significant changes thereafter.

120332227.text: Precisely. This is a terrible thing to be saying, but... I'm starting to have second thoughts. Maybe I went along with it all too easily. Maybe I allowed myself to be pushed into this...

120332228.text: Ah! I'm so sorry, I can't believe I'm making my guests listen to me complaining...

120332229.text: No problem at all. The Yashiro Commission has a duty to listen to you. Now that I've heard your concerns, I should offer to help you as best I can, for instance, by helping you gather your thoughts on the matter.

120332230.text: Now. We heard from Sir Kujou that his decision to tie the knot was prompted by a letter he received from you.

120332231.text: But we've also heard that you did not write that letter. Sir Kujou thought that perhaps you were just being coy... Oh dear, perhaps I should have kept that part to myself?

120332232.text: ...What? But that was... It was just a prop in his playful proposal, wasn't it? It was clearly purpose-designed, what with all the fancy lettering, and so on...

120332234.text: So I am to understand that had it not been for this letter, you two may not have chosen this moment to be wed?

120332235.text: When it comes down to it... Yes, I think so... Oh, do you mean to say that this letter is not what I thought it to be?

120332236.text: Sir Kujou maintains that the letter was penned by your hand.

120332238.text: Either way, it's wonderful to see how much you both trust one another. In that sense, you could say that the origin of the letter is ultimately not of great importance.

120332239.text: Who knows, perhaps Sir Kujou was the one being coy. After all, he had no particular reason to be forthcoming with us about the details of his playful proposal.

120332241.text: I understand. As you say, ultimately, the origin of the letter doesn't matter.

120332242.text: But my position does matter. Kamaji and I thought that we needn't worry about anything that lies ahead, because we can face it all together.

120332243.text: But now, I... I think I should give it some more thought.

120332244.text: Marriage is the most important decision of your life. Don't let yourself regret it.

120332245.text: It is also part of the Yashiro Commission's job to help people through difficult times.

120332246.text: I say this as an advocate for you personally and for the Hiiragi Clan. Please do not be compelled by circumstances to make any decision that goes against your will.

120332247.text: To be together with the one you love is a sacred thing. It is my earnest wish that both of you may enjoy a bright and beautiful future, not a bittersweet one.

120332248.text: I'll take to heart every word you have said to me... I can't thank you enough, Sir Kamisato. I'll think very carefully about your advice.

120332249.text: All that matters is that you follow your heart. Since you'll be needing some time to think things over, we will excuse ourselves now.

120332250.text: Ah, wait! Let me see you out...

120332251.text: Thank you, Lady Hiiragi, but there will be no need.

120332252.text: Traveler, let's find somewhere to talk.

subQuests.subQuestName: Leave the Hiiragi Estate and go over what you know

120332401.text: Hiiragi Chisato is on a totally different page than Kujou Kamaji...

120332402.text: Ayato, why did you give her such vague suggestions? Couldn't you just have told her what you'd do in her position? 'Cause Paimon's pretty sure you have an idea.

120332403.text: I've said everything I can, given the Yashiro Commission's stance. Interfering too much with other Commissions' domestic issues will only create trouble.

120332404.text: The more I think about it, the stranger this all seems, but Hiiragi Chisato has yet to see it. We must be vigilant.

120332406.text: Someone wants Hiiragi Chisato to be married as soon as possible, and if my guess is right... it is someone from within the Kanjou Commission. This person is presumably also responsible for the mysterious and misleading letter.

120332407.text: Think about this: A lowly officer is greatly worried about Hiiragi Chisato's future, while the heads of the supporting clans ostensibly have no concerns at all. It doesn't add up.

120332408.text: When someone's words and actions do not match, you need to infer their intentions from their behavior.

120332410.text: Yes. It's a smart strategy. Far superior to the one adopted by the Tenryou Commission's Takatsukasa Clan.

120332411.text: Even had the forged letter failed and been seen for what it was, there would have been no repercussions. They could simply have explained it away as a misguided but well-meaning matchmaking attempt by a member of the family.

120332412.text: But if the letter were to achieve its goal, as it has so far... the perpetrator would successfully weaken the Hiiragi Clan without ever having to lift a finger against them, all under the guise of simply encouraging a wedding.

120332413.text: With Hiiragi Chisato having married into the Kujou Clan and the head of the Hiiragi Clan in prison, challenges to the Hiiragi Clan's leadership would begin to emerge throughout the ranks of the Kanjou Commission... Eventually, another clan would take the Hiiragi Clan's place.

120330301.text: Not to pry, but it seems like there's something on your mind. Do you want to talk about it?

120330302.text: It's nothing. I just didn't sleep well, that's all. Really, I'm fine.

120330501.text: What's wrong? Are you worried about having to be on your best behavior around my lord? Hahaha, don't be nervous. He's actually pretty easy to get along with.

120330502.text: Well... the vast majority of the time, at least...

120331101.text: Now, where were we again? Ah yes, invitations...

120331102.text: My family can take charge of that. We have a lot of written correspondence with them already.

120331103.text: Sounds sensible to me. Then, thank you.

120331201.text: Ah, it's you two! Seems like you're always showing up with a VIP in tow.

120331202.text: I got my license and I'm doing a soft opening today. Wanna try out my latest creative drink?

120331203.text: I'm a little busy right now...

120331204.text: Okay sure. Well, feel free to swing by later if you're free.

120331302.text: Ah, it's you! Good to see you again.

120331303.text: Seems like you're always showing up with a VIP in tow.

120331304.text: Oh? So you know the owner as well?

120331401.text: I meant to ask earlier — do you know the owner here as well?

120331501.text: Yep! We tried his Dango Milk a while back with the Almighty Shogun in Inazuma City.

120331502.text: Ah, I see... So you were involved in that...

120331503.text: I'd caught wind of this Dango Milk, but I didn't know that it had anything to do with you two.

120331506.text: I always order one of his creative drinks whenever I pass the stall. The flavor is always new and interesting.

120331507.text: When I noticed he'd set up shop in Ritou, I simply had to come by.

120331508.text: Ah, thanks to you all, my business is finally beginning to take off. More and more people are willing to give my creative cuisine a shot.

120331509.text: It gave me the confidence to decide that I'm gonna stick to creative cuisine from now on.

120331510.text: On the one hand, I wanted more people to be able to try out my culinary creations. On the other hand, I wanted my customers to experience the joy of being creative, too.

120331511.text: So, I gave it a lot of thought, and finally came up with an all-new business concept.

120331512.text: Sounds interesting. What is it this time?

120331513.text: I've decided to give complete creative control to the customer. I offer all sorts of ingredients, and they pick and choose whatever they want to mix with their milk or tea.

120331514.text: As well as Dango, I now offer Rice Cake, Purple Potato Balls, Black Sugar, and Sunsettia.

120331515.text: Do they really all go well with milk...?

120331516.text: Hmm, hard to imagine. But... who knows — it could be delicious!

120331517.text: What if I were to choose some ingredients you don't have here? Would that be okay?

120331518.text: Uhh, well... I guess so. Any novel ideas you have, Commissioner, please feel free to tell me. I'll go buy the ingredients right away.

120331519.text: The whole idea was to let my customers express their creativity freely. So of course, I shouldn't place restrictions on the ingredients if I can help it.

120331520.text: Excellent. There are a few things I'd like to try...

120331521.text: Lavender Melon, Seagrass, and Sea Ganoderma.

120331522.text: Uh, what? You want to mix those with milk?

120331523.text: I do indeed — why, what's wrong?

120331524.text: ...You really think that's gonna turn out tasting good!?

120331525.text: It's all about the experience — the taste is secondary. It's great to try new things.

120331602.text: Sounds like a risky choice. Are you sure...? Well, okay, Paimon will have the same as you...

120331603.text: Three Milks with Lavender Melon, please.

120331604.text: No problem. Gimme a second, I'll have them ready in just a moment.

120331605.text: After a short while, the "Creative Milk" is finally ready.

120331606.text: Here, your milk is ready. Give it a try!

120331608.text: Yup, just as Paimon suspected. Raw Lavender Melon does not taste good!

120331609.text: I think it tastes alright. It makes me feel in touch with mother nature.

120331702.text: Are you serious? Uh... will Paimon seem like a scaredy-cat if she opts out of this one? Ugh, okay, Paimon'll have one, too...

120331704.text: No problem. Gimme a second, I'll have them ready in just a moment.

120331705.text: After a short while, the "Creative Milk" is finally ready.

120331706.text: Here, your milk is ready. Give it a try!

120331708.text: The Seagrass is stuck in the straw... Phew, this is so much work...

120331709.text: But it tastes alright. It captures the essence of the ocean.

120331803.text: Doesn't Paimon get a say in this? So this is peer pressure, huh? Well... Alright, then bring it on! Paimon can take it!

120331804.text: Three Milks with Sea Ganoderma, please.

120331805.text: No problem. Gimme a second, I'll have them ready in just a moment.

120331806.text: After a short while, the "Creative Milk" is finally ready.

120331807.text: Here, your milk is ready. Give it a try!

120331809.text: Somehow, Paimon got it down eventually, but... ugh, Paimon feels light-headed...

120331810.text: I think it's alright. It has quite a fascinating texture.

120331902.text: Yes! Dango! Dango will do nicely!

120331903.text: Hmm. An ordinary choice, but there's nothing wrong with that.

120331904.text: Two Dango Milks, and one Milk with Lavender Melon, please.

120331905.text: No problem. Gimme a second, I'll have them ready in just a moment.

120331906.text: After a short while, the "Creative Milk" is finally ready.

120331907.text: Here, your milk is ready. Give it a try!

120331908.text: Dango Milk tastes pretty good once you get used to it.

120331910.text: A most memorable texture indeed. A success, I'd say.

120332101.text: Thanks for coming. Hope to see you again!

120332102.text: Maybe this whole "creativity" theme really will work out...

120339901.text: Seems like you guys talked a lot without actually saying anything...

120339902.text: Hence why I dislike small talk.

120339903.text: Our timing was not ideal, but never mind. I spotted a stall on our way over where we can pass the time.

120339904.text: The owner always manages to come up with novel ideas. I'm one of his regular customers.
